_note: Historical pressure (scripts/sim/pressure.gd). Each event fires at the first month on or after `date` while its conditions hold, and is dropped once `until` has passed. The player is asked if they are an actor (a, or b with b_options; a `mirror` event reads the same from either side); otherwise the event is news and `ai_option` (or b_ai_option) is applied. Actors are tags, $player or a pick of what a nation is now (tension.picks); conditions: tension_min, tension_max, relation_above, peace, pressure_ai, player_great_power, no_great_war (no war between two great powers), after_great_war (once two great powers have fought a war to its end), months_from_start (not in the scenario's first months). Effects: tension, relation [a,b,d], treasury [a,m], prestige [a,n], war_support [a,n], points [a,n], manpower [a,fraction], mobilize [a,d], grievance [holder,target,n], treaty [kind,a,b,terms,note], war [a,b,(calls)].

tension._note: Tension (Pressure.parts): base + arms (growth of the great powers' men under arms over a base that starts at the scenario's armies and, once two great powers have fought a war to its end, moves arms_drift of the way to them each month, times arms_weight, at most arms_max) + mobilization (each great power's level above mobilization_from, times weight, at most max) + wars (war_each for every war a great power fights, at most war_max) + rivalry (the average dislike between the great powers times rivalry_weight) + the lingering force of events, which fades impulse_decay a month. From aggression_from the AI grows bolder, up to aggression_gain more aggression at 100. From harden_above the great powers' quarrels worsen harden_per_month a month. ai_war_gate: below this tension the AI starts no war of its own choosing (a war it was provoked into, or its allies' wars, are not held back). impulse_max caps what events can add. bloc_weight: added when the great powers stand in two alliance circles of at least two each.

appeals._note: Appeal (Pressure.appeal): a nation takes a public stand, one at a time (wait_days before it may take either again). cost is diplomacy points, prestige and war_support what the nation gains. A call for calm lowers tension by (tension + great_power for a great power + per_prestige times its prestige) times (0.5 + tension/100), at most tension_max (Pressure.appeal_tension); a rattled sabre adds its tension and costs neighbour_relation with every land neighbour.

calm.label: Appeal for calm
calm.tip: A speech and a note to the powers asking them to step back. It carries as much weight as your nation does.

rattle.label: Rattle the sabre
rattle.tip: Parades, speeches and a hard line: your people cheer, your neighbours take note and Europe frowns.

picks._note: Events may name a role by what a nation is now (Pressure._pick_role): $lost_ground (gave up ground at a peace in the last recent_months) and $winner (who took it), $empire (the most troubled of `empires`: war support under empire_support, or ground lost lately), $most_armed and $second_armed (the great powers with the most men under arms).

events.title: The Boxer Rising
events.text: The foreign legations in Peking are besieged. The powers are gathering an expedition, and {a}'s Kaiser wants his share of the glory.

options.label: Send an expedition
options.text: Troops and ships go east. It is costly, but the flag is seen.

options.label: Stay out
options.text: Let the others bear the cost.

events.title: Chamberlain's overture
events.text: Britain's colonial secretary hints at an understanding with Germany: a quiet alliance against Russia and France.

options.label: Pursue an understanding
options.text: Talk, and see what Berlin wants.

options.label: Keep our hands free
options.text: Splendid isolation has served well enough.

events.title: The end of splendid isolation
events.text: Britain stands alone in a world of alliances. The Boer War has shown how few friends it has.

options.label: Seek an understanding with Germany
options.text: A friendly hand across the North Sea.

options.label: Keep to isolation
options.text: Britain needs no friends.

options.label: Turn to France
options.text: Settle the old colonial quarrels.

events.title: The Anglo-Japanese Alliance
events.text: Britain, tired of standing alone in the Far East, can bind itself to Japan. The great powers take note that splendid isolation is ending.

options.label: Sign with Japan
options.text: Britain gains a partner in the East, and Russia a rival.

options.label: Decline
options.text: Keep both hands free.

events.title: The Boer War ends
events.text: The long, costly war in South Africa is over at last, and the army has been shown up badly.

options.label: Accept the peace
options.text: The treasury and the army's name pay for it.

events.title: The Triple Alliance is renewed
events.text: Italy is asked to renew the Triple Alliance. Rome has been quietly settling its quarrels with France.

options.label: Renew it, with a secret understanding with France
options.text: One foot in each camp.

options.label: Renew it without reservation
options.text: Loyal to Berlin and Vienna.

events.title: The Venezuela blockade
events.text: Germany and Britain are blockading Venezuelan ports to collect unpaid debts, and Washington is watching.

options.label: Join the blockade
options.text: Gunboats make a debtor pay.

options.label: Leave it to others
options.text: Not worth the quarrel with America.

events.title: The Baghdad Railway concession
events.text: The Sultan offers a German company the right to build a railway from Konya to the Persian Gulf.

options.label: Take the concession
options.text: German steel and German influence reach the Gulf.

options.label: Decline
options.text: The cost and the quarrel are not worth it.

events.title: The May Coup in Belgrade
events.text: Officers have murdered the king and queen of Serbia and put the rival Karageorgevic dynasty on the throne. Vienna's friends are gone from Belgrade.

options.label: Turn to Russia
options.text: The new king looks to St Petersburg and away from Vienna.

options.label: Keep a careful balance
options.text: Do not give Vienna a reason to act.

b_options.label: Cut Serbia down to size
b_options.text: A new, bolder Serbia must be shown its place.

b_options.label: Seek a quiet understanding
b_options.text: Serbia's new rulers can be won with trade.

events.title: The Mürzsteg agreement
events.text: Russia and Austria-Hungary, rivals in the Balkans, can agree on a joint programme of reform for Macedonia and keep the peace there.

options.label: Join the programme
options.text: A calm Balkans for a few years, and a little less distrust.

options.label: Go it alone
options.text: Russia will not share the Balkans.

events.title: The Anglo-French arbitration treaty
events.text: Britain and France, after Fashoda, can settle their disputes by arbitration instead of by threats.

options.label: Sign the treaty
options.text: Quarrels go to a judge, not to the fleets.

options.label: Hold off
options.text: Britain keeps its freedom of action.

events.title: War in the Far East
events.text: Russia is at war with Japan over Manchuria and Korea, and it is going badly for the Tsar's armies.

options.label: The war goes badly
options.text: Money, men and prestige drain away in the East.

events.title: Entente Cordiale
events.text: France and Britain, old rivals, are ready to settle their quarrels in Egypt and Morocco and to stand together against whatever comes.

options.label: Sign the entente
options.text: A friendship between the two powers, binding enough to matter.

options.label: Decline
options.text: Keep both hands free.

events.title: The Dogger Bank incident
events.text: A Russian fleet bound for the Far East has fired on British fishing boats in the North Sea. London is furious.

options.label: Apologize and pay
options.text: The fleet goes on, and the quarrel is smoothed over.

options.label: Deny it
options.text: Russia will not be called to account.

events.title: Revolution in Russia
events.text: Strikes and mutiny spread through the Tsar's empire after Bloody Sunday.

options.label: Grant a Duma
options.text: Reform, and a weaker Tsar.

options.label: Put it down by force
options.text: Order restored, anger stored up.

events.title: The Tangier visit
events.text: The Kaiser has landed at Tangier and declared for Moroccan independence. France sees a challenge to its place in Morocco.

options.label: Press the challenge
options.text: Germany will be heard in Morocco.

options.label: Let it pass
options.text: Do not push France to a point of no return.

b_options.label: Call for a conference
b_options.text: Let the powers settle it.

b_options.label: Stand firm and call up reserves
b_options.text: France will not bend.

b_options.label: Give way to Germany
b_options.text: Peace is worth a concession.

events.title: Norway and the union
events.text: Norway's parliament has ended the union with Sweden. Stockholm must decide whether to accept it.

options.label: Accept the dissolution
options.text: A peaceful parting.

options.label: Mobilize on the border
options.text: Sweden will not be dismissed.

b_options.label: Declare the union ended
b_options.text: Norway goes its own way.

b_options.label: Seek talks first
b_options.text: A quieter road to the same end.

events.title: The fall of Delcassé
events.text: Germany has made it plain that it will not tolerate the French foreign minister's Moroccan policy. Paris must decide whether he stays.

options.label: Let him go
options.text: Peace is worth a minister.

options.label: Back him
options.text: France will not take orders from Berlin.

events.title: The Treaty of Björkö
events.text: The Kaiser has met the Tsar on a yacht and proposes a pact that would draw Russia away from France.

options.label: Sign it
options.text: A pact of friendship between Berlin and St Petersburg.

options.label: Let it lapse
options.text: Ministers on both sides will not have it.

events.title: The Treaty of Portsmouth
events.text: American mediation has ended the war with Japan. Russia pays no indemnity, but the army and the treasury are exhausted.

options.label: Sign the treaty
options.text: Better peace abroad while the revolution burns at home.

events.title: The Schlieffen Plan
events.text: The German General Staff has a plan for a two-front war: knock France out through Belgium before Russia can mobilize.

options.label: Adopt the plan
options.text: The railways and the timetables are built around it.

options.label: Keep to defence
options.text: Germany will not plan to violate its neighbours.

events.title: The Algeciras Conference
events.text: The powers meet to settle Morocco. Germany finds that only Austria stands beside it.

options.label: Germany is isolated
options.text: The conference goes France's way.

events.title: HMS Dreadnought
events.text: Britain has launched a battleship that makes every other battleship obsolete. The naval race is on.

options.label: Build a dreadnought programme
options.text: Keep the lead at sea, whatever it costs.

options.label: Hold back
options.text: Spend the money elsewhere.

b_options.label: Pass a new Naval Law
b_options.text: Match them ship for ship.

b_options.label: Do not race
b_options.text: Germany's future is on land.

events.title: The Pig War
events.text: Austria-Hungary has shut its border to Serbian pigs, Serbia's main export, to bring Belgrade to heel.

options.label: Keep the border closed
options.text: Serbia must come to terms.

options.label: Compromise
options.text: Open the border on terms.

b_options.label: Look to other markets
b_options.text: Serbia turns to France and the Balkans.

b_options.label: Make terms with Vienna
b_options.text: The pigs go north again.

events.title: Persia's constitution
events.text: A revolution in Tehran has forced the Shah to grant a parliament, and the great powers circle.

options.label: Watch and wait
options.text: Keep the Shah's court close.

options.label: Back the Shah
options.text: A constitution so near the Caucasus is dangerous.

events.title: The Second Hague Conference
events.text: The Tsar has called the powers to The Hague to speak of arms limits and arbitration.

options.label: Press for disarmament
options.text: A moral lead, and a little less tension.

options.label: Send a token delegation
options.text: Say yes, and do nothing.

events.title: The Anglo-Russian Convention
events.text: Britain and Russia are ready to settle Persia, Afghanistan and Tibet, and with that, to stand near each other in Europe.

options.label: Sign the convention
options.text: With France, the three form a Triple Entente.

options.label: Decline
options.text: Keep free of continental quarrels.

events.title: Murder in Lisbon
events.text: King Carlos of Portugal and his heir have been shot in the street.

options.label: Crown the younger son
options.text: The monarchy goes on, shaken.

options.label: Make way for reform
options.text: The new government grants more than the old would.

events.title: The Young Turk Revolution
events.text: Officers in Salonika have forced the Sultan to restore the constitution. The Ottoman state is stirring, and its neighbours are watching.

options.label: A new government
options.text: Reform, and a weaker hold on the provinces.

events.title: The Buchlau bargain
events.text: Russia's foreign minister has told Austria-Hungary's that Russia will not object to the annexation of Bosnia, if the Straits are opened to Russian warships.

options.label: Bargain
options.text: Bosnia for the Straits.

options.label: Refuse
options.text: Russia will not trade Slav lands.

events.title: The Bosnian annexation
events.text: Austria-Hungary has annexed Bosnia and Herzegovina, which it has run since 1878. Serbia is outraged and looks to Russia.

options.label: Annex the provinces
options.text: The map changes on paper; the anger is real.

options.label: Postpone
options.text: Do not provoke the Slavs and Russia.

b_options.label: Protest and appeal to Russia
b_options.text: Serbia will not be ignored.

b_options.label: Accept it
b_options.text: Serbia cannot fight Austria alone.

events.title: The Daily Telegraph interview
events.text: The Kaiser has told an English newspaper that the English are mad as March hares, and that he is their friend. Neither side is pleased.

options.label: Defend the Kaiser
options.text: Germany will not apologize for its sovereign.

options.label: Rein him in
options.text: The Chancellor makes the Kaiser promise to hold his tongue.

events.title: Bulgaria declares itself a kingdom
events.text: With the Ottomans weakened, Prince Ferdinand has proclaimed full independence and made himself Tsar.

options.label: Proclaim the Tsardom
options.text: Bulgaria is its own master at last.

options.label: Wait
options.text: A better moment may come.

events.title: The Belgian Congo
events.text: The Congo Free State, the King's own, has become a scandal. Belgium may take it over, and Britain is watching.

options.label: Take it over as a colony
options.text: The state, not the King, is answerable.

options.label: Leave it to the King
options.text: Hope the scandal passes.

events.title: The ultimatum to Russia
events.text: Germany is asked to say whether it stands behind its ally in the Balkans.

options.label: Back Austria without reserve
options.text: Russia must yield, and remember it.

options.label: Counsel moderation
options.text: Germany does not want a war over Bosnia.

events.title: The Tragic Week in Spain
events.text: Calling up reservists for the war in Morocco has set Barcelona on fire.

options.label: Crush the rising
options.text: Order is restored, and the government's name is not.

options.label: Call off the reserves
options.text: Spain will not fight for Morocco at that price.

events.title: The Goudi coup
events.text: Greek officers have forced reform on the government and called Eleftherios Venizelos to Athens.

options.label: Reform the army and the state
options.text: A leaner, bolder Greece.

options.label: Put the officers in their place
options.text: The old order holds.

events.title: The Racconigi agreement
events.text: Italy and Russia agree to a pact over the Balkans, at Austria's expense. Italy's loyalty to the Triple Alliance wears thin.

options.label: Sign
options.text: Italy keeps a foot in each camp.

options.label: Decline
options.text: Loyal to Vienna and Berlin.

events.title: The Tegetthoff class
events.text: The Austro-Hungarian navy wants four dreadnoughts for the Adriatic, and Italy is watching the slipways.

options.label: Order the dreadnoughts
options.text: Prestige at sea, and a bill for the Delegations.

options.label: Defer the programme
options.text: The treasury cannot bear it.

events.title: The Albanian revolt
events.text: The mountain clans have risen against the new Ottoman levies and conscription.

options.label: Send the army
options.text: Crush it before it spreads.

options.label: Offer concessions
options.text: Schools in Albanian, and fewer tax collectors.

events.title: Montenegro becomes a kingdom
events.text: Prince Nicholas has crowned himself king of the little mountain state, which he has ruled for fifty years.

options.label: Take the crown
options.text: A flag and a title, and a larger idea of itself.

events.title: Dreadnoughts for the Adriatic
events.text: Austria-Hungary has laid down its first dreadnoughts, and Italy will not be outbuilt in the Adriatic.

options.label: Build the dreadnoughts
options.text: A navy to match the empire's pride.

options.label: Hold back
options.text: The money is wanted for the army.

b_options.label: Match them
b_options.text: Italy will not be second in its own sea.

b_options.label: Seek an understanding
b_options.text: A naval agreement in the Adriatic.

events.title: The march on Fez
events.text: French troops have gone to Fez to protect the Sultan of Morocco, and so, Berlin says, to take his country.

options.label: Occupy Fez
options.text: France will protect its interests in Morocco by force.

options.label: Hold the column back
options.text: Do not give Germany a pretext.

events.title: The Panther at Agadir
events.text: Germany has sent a gunboat to the Moroccan port of Agadir. France and Britain are alarmed.

options.label: Show the flag at Agadir
options.text: Demand compensation in the Congo.

options.label: Negotiate quietly
options.text: Take what can be had without a crisis.

b_options.label: Appeal to Britain
b_options.text: Britain's voice is worth a fleet.

b_options.label: Negotiate
b_options.text: Give a little to be rid of it.

b_options.label: Mobilize
b_options.text: Show them France will fight.

events.title: The war for Tripoli
events.text: Italy has attacked the Ottoman Empire for Tripoli and the Dodecanese. The Ottomans can do little to stop it.

options.label: Seize Tripoli
options.text: Glory and a colony, at a price.

options.label: Refrain
options.text: Keep the peace.

events.title: Stolypin is shot
events.text: Russia's reforming prime minister has been assassinated in Kiev. The land reform stalls and the court drifts.

options.label: Carry on
options.text: The reform has few friends left.

events.title: The Morocco–Congo treaty
events.text: After Agadir, France takes a protectorate in Morocco, and Germany takes a strip of the French Congo.

options.label: Accept the bargain
options.text: A swamp for a nation's pride.

options.label: Grumble and wait
options.text: The public is told it was a humiliation.

events.title: The Haldane mission
events.text: Britain offers to talk about the naval race with Germany. An agreement could ease the tension.

options.label: Seek an agreement
options.text: Slow the race by talking.

options.label: Refuse
options.text: The fleet will be as large as the Navy Laws say.

events.title: The Balkan League
events.text: Serbia, Bulgaria, Greece and Montenegro are talking of an alliance against the Ottomans.

options.label: Join the league
options.text: The four small kingdoms bind themselves together.

options.label: Stay apart
options.text: Keep out of it.

events.title: The army laws
events.text: Germany proposes a larger peacetime army. France will have to answer.

options.label: Pass the Army Law
options.text: More corps in the field, more money, more fear.

options.label: Hold the line
options.text: The army is large enough.

b_options.label: Three-Year Service Law
b_options.text: Keep the conscripts longer to match them.

b_options.label: Keep two years
b_options.text: The treasury cannot bear more.

events.title: The Home Rule bill
events.text: The Liberal government has introduced Home Rule for Ireland, and Ulster is drilling volunteers.

options.label: Press on
options.text: The Commons has its majority.

options.label: Seek a compromise
options.text: Exempt the north, and lose the Irish members' enthusiasm.

events.title: The naval understanding
events.text: Britain and France can divide the seas between them: the French fleet to the Mediterranean, the British to the North Sea.

options.label: Agree
options.text: The fleets are distributed, and the Entente becomes a plan.

options.label: Decline
options.text: Britain is not bound to anyone's fleet.

events.title: Crete and the Greek parliament
events.text: Cretan deputies have taken their seats in the Greek parliament in Athens, and the Ottomans cannot stop them.

options.label: Accept them
options.text: In Athens' eyes, Crete is Greek already.

options.label: Delay
options.text: Do not provoke the Porte before the League is ready.

events.title: The First Balkan War
events.text: The Balkan League declares war on the Ottoman Empire. Within weeks the Ottoman armies in Europe are reeling.

options.label: Declare war
options.text: The league marches.

options.label: Hold back
options.text: Not yet.

events.title: The Scutari crisis
events.text: Montenegro's army is besieging Scutari, and Austria-Hungary will not tolerate a Slav port on the Albanian coast.

options.label: Hold the siege
options.text: Montenegro has paid in blood for the town.

options.label: Yield to the Powers
options.text: A conference in London decides the town's fate.

events.title: The Treaty of London
events.text: The Ottomans give up almost all their land in Europe, and the victors fall out over the spoils.

options.label: Accept the loss
options.text: The Empire pulls back toward Constantinople.

events.title: The Baghdad Railway settlement
events.text: Britain and Germany can settle the railway to the Persian Gulf: a line in German hands, but its end in British waters.

options.label: Sign the settlement
options.text: Another quarrel less, in the year before the war.

options.label: Refuse
options.text: The line will not end in British waters on German terms.

events.title: The quarrel over the spoils
events.text: The Balkan allies cannot agree on how to share Macedonia, and Bulgaria feels cheated by Serbia and Greece.

options.label: Strike at Serbia
options.text: Take Macedonia by force before the others settle in.

options.label: Accept Russian arbitration
options.text: Let the Tsar decide.

events.title: Belgium's military service law
events.text: The shadow over Belgium has lengthened; the government proposes universal service to defend its neutrality.

options.label: Pass the law
options.text: Every Belgian man to serve, and a stronger neutral.

options.label: Rely on the guarantee
options.text: The powers have promised to defend Belgium.

events.title: Russia's Great Programme
events.text: The Tsar's ministers propose a vast programme of rearmament: more corps, more railways, a fleet in the Baltic.

options.label: Adopt it
options.text: By 1917 Russia will be a military giant.

options.label: Pare it down
options.text: The treasury cannot carry it all.

events.title: The Zabern affair
events.text: A lieutenant has insulted the people of an Alsatian town, and the army has taken their side against the civil authorities.

options.label: Stand by the army
options.text: The Reichstag protests and the army carries on.

options.label: Rebuke the officers
options.text: The Kaiser is displeased, the Reichstag appeased.

events.title: The Liman von Sanders mission
events.text: A German general is to command the Ottoman corps at Constantinople. Russia sees the Straits in German hands.

options.label: Send the mission
options.text: German officers at the Straits.

options.label: Scale it back
options.text: The post goes to a lesser rank.

events.title: The Curragh incident
events.text: Officers at the Curragh camp have said they would resign rather than march on Ulster.

options.label: Smooth it over
options.text: The officers keep their commissions.

events.title: Shots at Sarajevo
events.text: The heir to the Austro-Hungarian throne has been shot in Sarajevo by a Bosnian Serb. Vienna wants to make Serbia pay.

options.label: Send an ultimatum to Serbia
options.text: Demands no independent state could accept. The alliances start to move.

options.label: Seek a settlement
options.text: Hold the army back and talk.

b_options.label: Accept part of the demands
b_options.text: Humiliating, but it may keep the peace.

b_options.label: Reject the ultimatum
b_options.text: Serbia will not be a vassal.

events.title: The lost provinces
events.text: {a} has signed away ground to {b}, and the country will not forget it. Statues are draped in black; leagues for the lost provinces fill the halls.

options.label: Swear to win them back
options.text: The nation will remember, and so will {b}.

options.label: Accept the peace
options.text: Bitter, but the country needs quiet.

events.title: Unrest in the empire
events.text: The peoples of {a} stir: strikes, newspapers in a dozen languages, and men who speak of a state of their own.

options.label: Grant autonomy
options.text: Diets, schools and offices in their own tongues.

options.label: Send in the troops
options.text: Order first; the rest can wait.

events.title: A conference on armaments
events.text: The powers are asked to The Hague to limit their armies and fleets. {a}, with the largest army in Europe, is watched above all, and {b} next.

options.label: Agree to limits
options.text: A pledge to call up fewer men.

options.label: Refuse to bind our hands
options.text: No power limits ours.

events.title: The Danish West Indies
events.text: Washington offers to buy St Thomas, St John and St Croix. The islands cost more than they bring, but they are Danish.

options.label: Sell the islands
options.text: Money for the treasury, and a little less of a flag in the world.

options.label: Keep them
options.text: The Landsting will not sell Danes.

events.title: The defence of Copenhagen
events.text: The army wants the capital ringed with forts; the radicals say a small country's only defence is to offend no one, least of all {b}.

options.label: Fortify Copenhagen
options.text: Forts on land and sea, paid for over years.

options.label: Rely on neutrality
options.text: Give Berlin no reason to look north.

events.title: The optants of North Schleswig
events.text: Berlin offers to settle the status of the Danes of North Schleswig, if Copenhagen drops its claim.

options.label: Sign the convention
options.text: The Danes there get papers; the claim waits.

options.label: Keep the claim alive
options.text: Schleswig is Danish.

events.title: The Luxembourg railways
events.text: The lease that lets the German railways run the Grand Duchy's lines comes up for renewal. Paris and Brussels offer to run them instead.

options.label: Renew the German lease
options.text: The trains keep running, and Berlin is pleased.

options.label: Turn to Paris and Brussels
options.text: Less German, and less money.

events.title: A Grand Duchess
events.text: The Grand Duke is dying and leaves a daughter. Some in the Chamber want the constitution changed first.

options.label: Crown Marie-Adelaide
options.text: A young sovereign, and a Catholic one.

options.label: Reform the constitution first
options.text: Parliament before the throne.

events.title: The end in Aceh
events.text: Thirty years of war in northern Sumatra. Van Heutsz says one more campaign will finish it.

options.label: Finish the war
options.text: Columns into the hills, whatever it costs.

options.label: Make a settlement
options.text: Let the sultan keep his court.

events.title: A conference at The Hague
events.text: The powers will meet again at The Hague to talk of arbitration and the laws of war, and the Netherlands is asked to host them.

options.label: Host the conference
options.text: A Peace Palace, and the world's eyes on The Hague.

options.label: Leave it to others
options.text: Nothing of the kind changes anything.

events.title: The forts of Flushing
events.text: The army wants to fortify Flushing at the mouth of the Scheldt. London says it would close Antwerp to a British army; Berlin says it is the Netherlands' own business.

options.label: Fortify Flushing
options.text: The Scheldt is Dutch.

options.label: Drop the plan
options.text: Neutral means offending no one.

events.title: The secret treaty
events.text: Romania's alliance with {b} is a secret even from most of the cabinet. It comes up for renewal while the papers cry for Transylvania.

options.label: Renew the secret treaty
options.text: The King keeps his word to Vienna.

options.label: Let it lapse
options.text: Look east instead.

events.title: The peasants rise
events.text: In Moldavia the peasants burn the manors of the leaseholders, and the fire spreads south.

options.label: Send in the army
options.text: Order, at the price of thousands dead.

options.label: Promise land reform
options.text: Cheaper rents and new laws.

events.title: The new army law
events.text: A new military organization: longer training, a modern artillery, and a vote of the people to approve it.

options.label: Adopt the law
options.text: The militia trained like an army.

options.label: Keep the old militia
options.text: Cheaper, and Swiss enough.

events.title: The Gotthard convention
events.text: Berlin and Rome want lasting rights on the Gotthard line in return for what they paid to build it. In the cantons they call it a sale of the Alps.

options.label: Sign the convention
options.text: Good relations, and a storm at home.

options.label: Refuse it
options.text: The Gotthard is Swiss.

events.title: A guarantee for Norway
events.text: The powers offer the new kingdom a treaty that promises its borders, if it gives up nothing for it.

options.label: Sign the treaty
options.text: Friends in London and Berlin alike.

options.label: Stand alone
options.text: Norway asks no one's leave.

events.title: The farmers' march
events.text: Thirty thousand farmers march on the palace to ask for armoured ships against {b}; the Liberal ministry wants to cut the budget.

options.label: Build the armoured ships
options.text: The King sides with the farmers.

options.label: Keep the budget cut
options.text: Defence within means.

events.title: The republic
events.text: Sailors and soldiers rise in Lisbon. The King is at the palace; the city is with the republicans.

options.label: Accept the republic
options.text: The King sails for England.

options.label: Defend the throne
options.text: The loyal regiments march.

events.title: Spain at Algeciras
events.text: The powers meet at Algeciras over Morocco. {b} wants Spain at its side; {c} wants a Spain that owes Paris nothing.

options.label: Side with France
options.text: A share of Morocco's police, and a friend across the Pyrenees.

options.label: Keep both at arm's length
options.text: Spain has had enough of other people's wars.

events.title: Independence at Vlore
events.text: With the Balkan armies closing in, the notables meet at Vlore and raise a flag of their own.

options.label: Declare independence
options.text: An Albania of the Albanians.

options.label: Wait for the powers
options.text: Let the conference in London decide.

events.title: A great power comes courting
events.text: {b} offers a loan on easy terms and officers to train the army, and wants a friend on the map for it.

options.label: Accept the loan and the mission
options.text: Money and instructors, and a patron.

options.label: Keep strict neutrality
options.text: Thank them, and owe no one.

events.title: A trade treaty
events.text: {b} offers to cut its tariffs on our goods if we cut ours on its manufactures.

options.label: Sign the treaty
options.text: Cheaper goods and a bigger market, and our workshops hurt.

options.label: Protect our industry
options.text: Our tariffs, our factories.

events.title: Trouble on the border
events.text: Soldiers of {b} crossed the border in pursuit of smugglers and arrested two of our customs men.

options.label: Protest loudly
options.text: A note, a speech, the press with us.

options.label: Settle it quietly
options.text: Apologies on both sides; the men come home.
